case_title: Ravindra Tukaram Hiwale v. State of Maharashtra
mitigating_circumstances: Incident spontaneous, arising from a family quarrel that morning; no misbehaviour by the accused over a period of time (trial court finding)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498-A IPC, one year RI; convicted under s.306 IPC, four years RI
high_court_outcome: Accused's appeal dismissed; State's appeal allowed; s.306 sentence enhanced from four to six years
offence_finally_established: IPC s.306 (abetment of suicide); IPC s.498-A (cruelty)
neutral_facts: The victim, a married woman, suffered serious burn injuries in the kitchen of the marital house at about 7.00 a.m. on 6 February 1990 and later died of those injuries. The prosecution case is that the victim had quarrelled with the accused, her husband, that morning over household chores and the feeding of the children. She then poured kerosene on herself and set herself alight. About three days after the burn injuries were sustained, at about 8.30 a.m. on 9 February 1990, the victim made a statement to a police head constable (PW.10), described as a dying declaration. In that statement she recounted the quarrel over household chores and the feeding of the children, and said that she had thereafter poured kerosene on herself and burnt herself. The prosecution relies on this declaration as the central evidence of how the burning occurred and of the events that morning. The accused and the victim had been married after the death of the accused's first wife.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from serious burn injuries
premeditation_planning: No premeditation or planning found; incident treated as spontaneous (trial court finding accepted by the Supreme Court)
motive: Family quarrel on the morning of the incident over household chores and feeding of the children
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration recorded by PW.10 (police head constable) on 9 February 1990, and the trial court's finding that the incident was spontaneous
witness_credibility: Not stated; the court did not separately assess witnesses and relied on the dying declaration
custody_duration: About four years of sentence undergone, as reported by the learned amicus curiae; accused in custody
bail_history: Not stated; Supreme Court directed release forthwith if not required in any other case
trial_duration: offence: 6 February 1990 (burn injuries) / 9 February 1990 (dying declaration); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 02.08.2006; Supreme Court: 2 August 2010
legal_representation: Accused: B. Sridhar (appellant's counsel), with the learned amicus curiae referred to by the court; State of Maharashtra: Shankar Chillargee, Asha G. Nair, Ravindra Keshavrao Adsure
investigation_status: Dying declaration recorded by a police head constable (PW.10); trial completed with a trial court judgment; other investigation steps not stated
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.498-A (one year) and s.306 (four years). High Court: accused's appeal dismissed; State's appeal allowed, s.306 sentence enhanced to six years. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, High Court's enhanced sentence quashed, trial court judgment confirmed
prosecution_argument: Not stated; the order records only the appellant's submission
defence_argument: The High Court wrongly enhanced the sentence based on a quarrelsome nature shown by two letters written about a year before the incident
legal_principle_applied: Appellate interference with quantum of sentence should be rare and only in exceptional cases; sentencing discretion within the statutory range rests with the trial court; older letters carry little weight against a dying declaration
sentencing_rationale: Trial court's sentence restored: incident was spontaneous and arose from a morning family quarrel, with no misbehaviour over time; the High Court's reliance on older letters had little value; the incident occurred in February 1990 and the accused had served about four years
judicial_mitigating_factors: Spontaneous incident arising from a morning family quarrel; no misbehaviour over a period of time; about four years of sentence already undergone
other_sentence_order: Accused to be released forthwith if not required in connection with any other case
